blocks.text: RIID-6140: An owner connection failure is retried only before initialize or queue/start is sent, at most three connections within the existing five-second deadline, with cancellable backoff. After a typed owner-connect failure, only an explicit deleted=true acknowledgement for our queued submission permits thread/resume on the same native ID. If the writer is still active, retain the original request and client identity, announce connection wait once, and retry history/queue inspection after cancellable exponential backoff of 2, 4, 8, then 10 seconds. Only the confirmed deletion permits adding the same unstarted request again. Missing, malformed, failed or already-consumed deletion never permits replay. A known reconnect wait has semantic-idle grace until control connectivity or writer ownership recovers; the overall hard deadline and cancellation still win. Once execution starts, normal semantic-idle rules apply. This recovers transient socket outages and owner-release races, not a permanently stdio-only owner; Riido never terminates the owner, changes its locks, forks or starts an owner daemon. A released session uses the existing daemon resume parameters; a live owner retains its execution policy.
C4 Provider Runtime owns the provider session table that maps provider-native session identity to Riido runtime identity. C5 Scheduling owns task claim lease and heartbeat semantics, not this table.

rows: IR `SessionPinned` event payload plus C5 lease metadata runtime pin

items: Adapters do not keep session id as hidden private memory; they emit it as a draft for ingest.

Codex resume selects a locally installed executable with the original capability fingerprint for this submission only. New bindings retain a local executable hint. Older bindings can recover the provider version from the original run journal. Workspace, task, agent and repository grants are verified before resume.
Crash resume is recovered from the IR log plus provider session table.
The minimal session table key is `(ProviderSessionID, RuntimeID)`.
Runtime eligibility, lease expiry, stale fingerprint, and task handoff are still owned by C5/C9.

When Codex thread/resume reports an active writer for the requested native ID, the adapter validates that thread, imports completed external history, and uses the official thread/queue API. The supervisor-validated task working directory is carried explicitly in the queued prompt because the desktop may select a different cwd when opening a saved chat. The Codex desktop app remains the execution owner; Riido never forks, rewrites locks, or replaces its permissions or tools.

A stable clientUserMessageId identifies the Riido request. Queue recovery and result polling match this ID, never the latest turn or prompt text. Polling runs on the session actor through an optional provider protocol port; no driver goroutine mutates protocol state.

A queue/add acknowledgement proves storage, not execution. For a new or recovered pending submission, C4 explicitly calls thread/queue/start with that exact submission ID on the existing owner's control socket through codex app-server proxy. The bounded connection performs only initialize and queue/start; it never resumes the thread, changes settings, starts a daemon, or sends an uncorrelated turn/start. The private WebSocket exchange uses the standard library, with frame, message and time limits and no compression or remote endpoint.

An active-turn rejection waits for idle history and rechecks the same queue entry before another start attempt. A consumed entry is reconciled by clientUserMessageId, never resubmitted. If the owner cannot be reached or rejects the operation, remove only the acknowledged pending entry. A confirmed deletion means the request did not start. If deletion reports that the entry is already gone, reconcile by clientUserMessageId under the existing idle and hard deadlines instead of reporting failure or submitting again. A failed or malformed cleanup must tell the user to inspect the app queue before retrying. Report only fixed, non-sensitive connection, initialization, start rejection, or unconfirmed-start codes; never expose raw provider errors. An active writer can be a stdio-only app-server without an accessible control socket. An unreachable owner keeps the original Riido request waiting for automatic reconnection after confirmed cleanup. Riido does not require quitting Codex or resubmitting the reply for transient recovery. A permanently inaccessible stdio owner that retains the writer lock still cannot be controlled externally; waiting cannot promise execution before the hard deadline. Releasing that thread or restoring the control socket can recover while the owner process stays alive. Closing the control connection never stops the owner or its active turn.

Acceptance: a real native owner plus a detached Riido session must reproduce the old queue-only semantic idle timeout and complete the same-thread follow-up after the explicit start. Automated regression checks cover new and recovered submissions, active-turn races, missing owner, uncertain acknowledgement, own-entry cleanup, bounded malformed/oversized transport, and unchanged permissions. No task payload, credentials, provider installation, desktop updater, or watchdog deadline is changed; rollback is a daemon binary rollback without data migration.

Disk-backed Codex reads can label a running turn interrupted. Shared-writer results require a completedAt timestamp as well as a terminal status. Only the matching request supplies live output and a terminal result; other completed messages enter the existing native-history import path.

Cancellation removes only this request's pending queue entry and waits for its acknowledgement within a bounded cleanup deadline. An already consumed request remains owned by the Codex app: Riido reports that execution must be stopped there and stops observing it. Unsupported queue APIs fail explicitly without creating another thread or retrying submission blindly.

blocks.text: Native shared-owner regression: RIIDO_CODEX_NATIVE_TEST_EXECUTABLE=/absolute/path/to/codex go test ./internal/provider/codex -run '^TestIntegrationShared' -count=1 -v. The fixture creates an isolated Codex home, a native owner and detached Riido session, and a localhost model stub; it does not use user threads, provider credentials or external tools. The fixture checks the same thread ID, exactly one follow-up, owner survival, and preserved read-only/on-request settings. Additional fixtures verify control recovery after repeated connection failures and automatic same-thread execution after a stdio owner unsubscribes and releases its idle thread without exiting. A permanently retained stdio owner reaches the hard deadline with no extra model call, duplicate request or leftover queue entry. Fake-clock tests cover backoff, cancellation, stable identity, and ending idle grace when execution starts. A lost start acknowledgement with a consumed queue entry must recover the matching result without another write. Ordinary CI also runs the queue recovery, cancellation, failure cleanup and bounded control-transport tests without a native installation.

items: An owned Codex run pins the thread from the correlated thread/start or thread/resume reply and the turn from its turn/start reply. Child or stale thread/turn notifications cannot change session identity, assistant output, runtime errors, or terminal state. Notifications arriving before the turn reply are bounded and replayed only after correlation; missing identity in a modern owned stream is not terminal evidence. Legacy replies without a turn ID retain the legacy stream contract.

A Codex wait item from the owned thread and turn identifies its delegated targets. Starting or completing that wait, or receiving text or completed work from an active target turn, refreshes semantic idle. The daemon records wait lifecycle and target IDs. Delegated content stays private to Codex; unrelated, stale, or silent threads do not extend the deadline.

An identified modern run completes from its correlated terminal event or a bounded read of the same completed native turn at semantic idle. Thread status alone cannot override interrupted/failed turn status. Server tool approval requests retain their exact RPC identity, including delegated child requests; run-output isolation does not silently discard approvals.

Final Riido output is selected from parent agentMessage items marked final_answer. Commentary and unknown-phase deltas report progress without becoming final output; phase-less legacy item streams use the last completed agent message. Shared-owner polling follows the same final-answer selection. Failure or interruption retains its actual status, including after partial output.

Owned terminal and rejected terminal events record the target thread/turn, event thread/turn, method and decision reason without message bodies or credentials. At semantic idle, the session may issue one read-only Codex thread/read before terminating the process. Recovery requires the pinned thread and turn, a completed status with a completion timestamp, and a final answer. Cancellation and hard deadlines still preempt recovery. Process exit without owned terminal evidence is a failure, even after partial output. Acceptance replays child completion followed by parent posting/finalization through the real session and verifies no early process kill, parent-only result, stale/missing IDs, early notifications, failed/interrupted status, and shared-owner regression. No provider permissions, task claims, updater contracts or data migrations change; rollback is a daemon binary rollback.
